site.name: runeforge-docs
site.summary: runeforge-docs Fictional state-management JavaScript library "Runeforge" official documentation site (Redux / Zustand-style ergonomics). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Sticky topbar with brand+version pill, doc tabs, ⌘K search trigger, version selector, theme toggle, GitHub stars; **three-column layout**: left categorized TOC tree (5 sections, 26 items), center page with hero / install code-tabs (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun) / "Hello, store" code-tabs (5 framework adapters: Vanilla / React / Solid / Svelte 5 / Vue 3) with copy button / 3-tile "three things to remember" / 6-row why-table comparing to Redux / Zustand / Jotai / next-steps list / prev/next pager; right-side on-this-page TOC. - `guide-quickstart.html` — 5-minute tutorial. Step-by-step build of a counter store, todo list with derived store, async fetcher with `asyncSlice()`, and devtools install. Lots of code blocks and an info / success callout. - `guide-stores.html` — Stores reference. Store API table; reading + subscribing; immutability warning callout; composing with `derive()`; slicing with `store.select()`; SSR (`toJSON` / `fromJSON`); testing pattern. - `guide-actions.html` — Actions & selectors. Action rules; selector c

run_plan.goal: Critique the UX of the Runeforge documentation system with emphasis on the primary “getting started → quickstart” learning flow and adjacent reference/example flows, including recovery paths (search, versioning, navigation) and mobile usability.
run_plan.summary: Run through the documented user journeys starting at index.html, then validate the quickstart and core-concepts pages (Stores, Actions & selectors) for navigability, code-block usability (tabs/copy), and clarity of callouts. Then test the adjacent flows: Examples filtering, API reference navigation, and any recovery paths via global search (⌘K) and version switching. Repeat the highest-risk checks on mobile (responsive layout, small tap targets, search + code interactions).
assumptions: The site is a local static build (file://) with working internal navigation between the listed HTML pages.
The global documentation UI on each page includes the sticky topbar (version selector, theme toggle, GitHub stars) and the ⌘K search trigger.

The primary interaction patterns visible in the prescan include: doc tab/navigation links, a version selector (select), a theme toggle button (☾), code-tabs with a copy button, and (on examples) an examples filter input plus category buttons.
No external network calls are required for interactions in this run; validation focuses on UI state changes rather than actual GitHub/forum content.
risk_hotspots: Global search trigger (⌘K) and its modal/panel behavior (focus management, keyboard shortcut, results navigation) — missing_input_label + small tap-target warnings near topbar controls.
Version selector (<select>) in the topbar (no accessible label per prescan warning) — validate discoverability, persistence, and that versioned content changes correctly.
Theme toggle button (☾) and its tap target size — validate state persistence and contrast/readability after toggle.
Code-tabs + Copy buttons on index.html and quickstart.html (copy action feedback, tab switching, code selection/copy correctness).
Three-column layout responsiveness: left TOC tree, center content, right on-this-page TOC — validate usability on mobile (potential overlaps and scroll locking).

Examples page filter input “Filter 12 examples…” plus category buttons (All/Beginner/Intermediate/Advanced) — validate filtering logic and empty-state/keyboard access (small tap-target + missing label risk).
API reference navigation within the right/left TOCs — validate anchored scrolling and that active section highlighting updates reliably.
Mobile tap targets: brand pill, nav links, and other small controls flagged in prescan as below 44px guidance.

phases.title: On-ramp validation: index.html (navigation + code usability)
phases.objective: Confirm the primary entry page supports an efficient path into Quickstart, and that core topbar/search/version/code interactions are usable and accessible.
key_checks: Use left TOC to jump from “Introduction” to “Quickstart (5 min)” and verify scroll/active state (URL hash or equivalent) without losing context.

Switch code-tabs in the “Install” area (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun) and “Hello, store” adapter tabs (Vanilla / React / Solid / Svelte 5 / Vue 3); verify active tab styling and that the correct snippet is shown.

Click the code-block Copy button and verify visible feedback (toast/label change) and that it copies the correct current snippet (as evidenced by UI feedback and/or system clipboard confirmation if available).
Open global search via ⌘K button and/or keyboard; validate search input appears, focus is trapped/released correctly, and search results can be clicked to navigate to a relevant section.
Change version via topbar select (v3.4 (latest) → v3.3/v2) and validate content updates consistently (or confirm intended behavior if some pages are static).
Toggle theme (☾) and verify typography/code contrast remains readable, and controls remain usable afterward.
exit_criteria: Quickstart is reachable from index via nav/TOC within 1–2 interactions and lands at the correct section.
At least one code-tab switch and one Copy interaction work with clear UI feedback.
Search modal/panel opens/closes reliably and navigation from a result works.
Version switching produces a visible content/state change or an explicit limitation is confirmed without breaking layout.
Theme toggle maintains readable contrast without broken controls.

phases.title: Primary learning flow: guide-quickstart.html (step execution + recovery)
phases.objective: Evaluate the Quickstart’s step-by-step guidance, especially code-block interaction patterns, callout comprehension, and intra-page navigation.
key_checks: Scan the five steps (Install → Counter → Todo derived store → Async via asyncSlice() → Devtools) using the right “on this page” list; verify each item scrolls to the correct step.
Validate info/success callouts: ensure styling hierarchy makes the intended emphasis clear and doesn’t hide content on scroll.
Switch any framework adapters inside the quickstart (if present) or validate that code blocks match the selected version/framework context shown in the rest of the site.
Trigger copy on multiple code blocks (at least one from each of: install and a later step such as async fetcher) and confirm feedback is consistent.
Use topbar search to find a keyword from Quickstart (e.g., “asyncSlice”, “devtools”, “derived”) and confirm results point back into Quickstart or the relevant guide section.
exit_criteria: All major Quickstart steps can be reached via the “on this page” navigation and are correctly aligned.
Copy feedback is consistent across multiple blocks.
Search can successfully locate at least one Quickstart-specific concept.
No layout break occurs during scroll/copy/tab switching.

phases.title: Core concepts depth: guide-stores.html + guide-actions.html (tables/callouts + rules clarity)
phases.objective: Validate that the Stores and Actions & selectors pages are navigable and that complex explanations (immutability warning, rules of thumb, selectors composition) are structured for understanding.
key_checks: On Stores: verify you can reach “Creating a store”, “Reading and subscribing”, “Composing stores”, and “Slicing a store” via right/left TOCs and that the active section updates.
Identify and interact with any callout warning (immutability warning mentioned in prescan summary for these docs) and verify it stands out and remains readable.
On Stores: validate any SSR serialization/recovery snippets are reachable and their code tabs/copy controls (if present) function.
On Actions & selectors: validate “Rules of thumb”, “Composing selectors”, and “Action middleware” sections are scannable.
Use topbar search to find a term from these pages (e.g., “derive”, “store.select”, “middleware”) and confirm the results navigation works.
exit_criteria: Key sections on both pages are reachable quickly via TOCs without mis-scrolling.
Any visible warning/callout remains legible and not obscured by fixed UI.
Search finds at least one concept from each page and navigates correctly.

phases.title: Adjacent reference & examples: api-reference.html + examples.html (filtering + deep links)
phases.objective: Test non-primary flows: API reference browsing and examples exploration with filtering; validate that navigation and UI state remain stable with version/theme/search.
key_checks: API reference: use the left/center reference nav to jump between functions (forge(), derive(), use(middleware), asyncSlice(), listSlice(), formSlice(), devtools()); verify anchors and active state.
API reference: validate any error/code blocks are readable and code-copy controls (if present) work (at least one interaction).
Examples: use the “Filter 12 examples…” input to filter (e.g., type “todo”, “async”, “ssr”) and verify the list updates (and handles no results if applicable).
Examples: click category chips/buttons (All / Beginner / Intermediate / Advanced) and verify filtering state is consistent with the filter text (and can be reset).
Examples: open at least one example’s fork/clone link or section navigation control (as visible in prescan) and verify it behaves as expected (or gracefully indicates non-availability).
exit_criteria: API reference anchors and active navigation highlight update correctly across multiple sections.
Examples filtering works for both text input and category selection with consistent state behavior.
At least one examples navigation/control works without breaking layout.

phases.title: Mobile usability pass (responsive + tap-target + search + code interactions)
phases.objective: Repeat the highest-risk interactions on a mobile viewport to catch responsive layout and accessibility regressions.
key_checks: Validate the three-column layout collapses appropriately (TOC handling, content readability) without overlapping essential controls.
Attempt topbar search (⌘K/controls if available) and confirm the search UI is usable with touch and keyboard equivalents.
Change version and toggle theme on mobile; confirm the controls remain reachable and readable.
Interact with code-tabs and Copy on mobile (tab switching + copy feedback) and verify target sizes and tap accuracy.
Examples page: use the filter input and category buttons on mobile; validate that the input is usable (no missing label issues impacting usability) and that button taps are not overly small.
exit_criteria: No critical UI elements become inaccessible on mobile (search/version/theme/filter/code copy).
All repeated interactions (search, code-tabs+copy, examples filtering) work on mobile.
TOCs do not obstruct content during scroll and navigation.

coverage_targets.features: exercise most visible controls per key page: topbar nav, ⌘K search, version selector, theme toggle, code-tabs (npm/adapters) and Copy, Quickstart step navigation, right on-this-page TOC, API reference anchor navigation, Examples filter input + category buttons
coverage_targets.mobile: repeat the critical checks on mobile for: search, version/theme toggle, code-tabs+copy, Quickstart step navigation, and Examples filter/category interactions

notes: Do not claim backend/API/real clipboard correctness beyond what the UI confirms; focus on observable UI state changes and feedback.
If version switching does not actually alter content in the static build, document the limitation while still validating that the control itself remains stable (no layout break).

Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Core concepts › Stores Core concept Stores. A store is the unit of state in Runeforge. It owns a single piece of state, exposes actions to update it, and notifies subscribers when it changes. Stores are framework-agnostic — they have no knowledge of React, Solid, or any UI library. Creating a store Use forge() to create one. observation.visible_text:
Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Getting started › Quickstart Quickstart · 5 minutes From zero to a working app. In the next five minutes you'll install Runeforge, build a counter, build a todo list, and wire up an async fetcher. By the end you'll have used 90% of the API. Prerequisites: Node 20+ (or Bun). The examples use React but everything maps 1:1 to Solid, Svelte, Vue, and vanilla JS. Step 1 · Install Create a fresh app with whatever template you like. Then install Runeforge and the React adapter. # inside your app directory npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Step 2 · A counter store The smallest useful store has one piece of state and one action. Both are inferred from the object you pass to forge(). // stores/counter.ts import { forge } from "runeforge"; export const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { increment: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), decrement: (s) => ({ count: s.count - 1 }), reset: () => ({ count: 0 }), }, }); Use it in a component with useStore: // Counter.tsx import { useStore } from "@runeforge/react"; import { counter } from "./stores/counter"; export function Counter() { const count = useStore(counter, (s) => s.count); return (

{count}

); } Notice three things: No provider. The store is just an import — it's already global. The component subscribes to a selector (s.count), not the whole store. If another part of state changed, this component would not re-render. Actions are called like ordinary methods. There's no dispatch(). Effects can read and write any store, await whatever they want, and report status into a status field. observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

Every one of them is under 500 lines and uses just the public API. Clone the repo, npm i, npm dev — that's the whole setup. All (12) Beginner Intermediate Advanced SSR beginner Counter (the canonical hello-world) The smallest possible Runeforge app. Single store, three actions, one component. React 34 LOC beginner Todo list with persistence Add / toggle / delete todos. State persists to localStorage with one option. React 88 LOC beginner Async fetcher with retry asyncSlice() pattern. Loads users with exponential-backoff retry on failure. Vue 3 110 LOC intermediate Multi-step form (typed) Uses formSlice() to manage values, errors, touched state, and submission. React 210 LOC intermediate Optimistic comments Show comments instantly, roll back on server error. Uses derive() + middleware. Solid 180 LOC intermediate Realtime presence WebSocket push updates per-user presence and merges into store. Svelte 5 240 LOC intermediate Routing-aware state Read URL params into a store; navigation is just an action. React 160 LOC advanced Undo / redo with snapshots Time-travel using built-in snapshot support. Cmd-Z / Cmd-Shift-Z. React 320 LOC advanced Server-side rendered shop Full SSR + hydration of multiple stores. Includes server-only state. React (Next 15) 460 LOC advanced Markdown editor with autosave Debounced autosave middleware, file-system adapter, and conflict detection. Vanilla JS 420 LOC advanced Spreadsheet with cross-cell formulas Each cell is a derived store; recompute graph triggered by edits. Solid 480 LOC advanced Drag-and-drop kanban (SSR) Move cards between columns; renders identically on server and client. React (Next 15) 440 LOC

observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.title: Runeforge — predictable state for JavaScript
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components PATTERNS Form state Optimistic updates Server data & cache Undo / redo Routing-aware state REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Introduction Getting started Predictable state, one rune at a time. Runeforge is a 4 kB state-management library for JavaScript apps. It gives you a single API — forge() — that works the same in vanilla JS, React, Solid, Svelte, and Vue. There are no providers, no boilerplate, no proxies. Just stores, actions, and subscriptions. Brand new? The 5-minute quickstart walks you through building a counter, a todo list, and an async fetcher. You'll write less code than any state library you've used before. Install Runeforge is published to npm under the same name. The core package has zero dependencies. Each framework adapter is its own ~1 kB package. npm pnpm yarn bun Copy # Core + React adapter (most common) npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Hello, store. Every Runeforge app starts with a forge() call. You pass it the initial state and a map of actions. You get back a store with get(), set(), subscribe(), and your action methods. Vanilla JS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Copy import { forge } from "runeforge"; const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), }, }); counter.subscribe((s) => document.title = `Count: ${s.count}`); counter.inc(); // Count: 1 Three things to remember Runeforge keeps the surface area tiny. Once you understand these three concepts, the rest is composition: 01 Stores hold state A store is the unit of state. Read with get(), write with set(), observe with subscribe(). Stores compose; you can derive one store from another. Read about stores → 02 Actions describe changes Actions are plain functions on a store. They get the current state and return the next state. There is no reducer, no dispatch, no string types. Read about actions → 03 Selectors keep components tiny Selectors derive computed values without re-renders. Components subscribe to a selector, not to the whole store, so they only update when the slice they care about changes. Read about selectors → Why another state library? Runeforge sits between two extremes. Redux makes every state change explicit and traceable but takes a lot of boilerplate. Signal-based libraries are very ergonomic but rely on framework-specific reactivity. Runeforge is framework-agnostic and explicit, but with a much smaller surface than Redux. RUNEFORGE REDUX TOOLKIT ZUSTAND JOTAI Bundle size (min+gz) 4.0 kB 13.6 kB 1.6 kB 3.9 kB Framework-agnostic Yes No (React-first) React-first React-only TypeScript inference Full Manual types Full Atom-by-atom Devtools Built-in (1 kB) External External External SSR / serialization First-class Manual Manual Manual Time-travel Yes Yes No No Next steps Build something in 5 minutes with the quickstart. Understand the model in Stores and Actions & selectors. Look up exact signatures in the API reference. See a working app in Examples. NEXT Quickstart → ON THIS PAGE Introduction Install Hello, store. Three things to remember Why another state library? Next steps Edit this page on GitHub → Discuss on the forum

observation.title: Stores — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Core concepts › Stores Core concept Stores. A store is the unit of state in Runeforge. It owns a single piece of state, exposes actions to update it, and notifies subscribers when it changes. Stores are framework-agnostic — they have no knowledge of React, Solid, or any UI library. Creating a store Use forge() to create one. The shape of the object you pass is the API of the store. import { forge } from "runeforge"; const session = forge({ state: { user: null as User | null, expiresAt: 0 }, actions: { login: (s, user: User, ttl: number) => ({ user, expiresAt: Date.now() + ttl }), logout: () => ({ user: null, expiresAt: 0 }), }, }); The returned store is a plain object with these methods, plus your actions as methods: MEMBER SIGNATURE DESCRIPTION get () => State Returns the current state (a frozen snapshot). set (next: Partial<State>) => void Imperative state update. Prefer actions in most cases. subscribe (listener) => unsubscribe Calls listener on every committed state change. select (selector) => SelectedView Returns a derived view that's its own subscribable store. reset () => void Returns to the initial state. Useful in tests. name string Auto-derived debug name, or passed via the options bag. Reading and subscribing The simplest store is read with get() and observed with subscribe(): const current = session.get(); // { user: null, expiresAt: 0 } const off = session.subscribe((next, prev) => { console.log("changed:", prev, "→", next); }); // later off(); State is immutable. Each commit replaces the previous state with a new frozen object. Don't try to mutate s.user.name = "x" — return a new object instead. Runeforge will warn in dev if it detects an in-place mutation. Composing stores Apps usually have several stores. They compose by importing each other and using derive(): import { derive } from "runeforge"; import { session } from "./session"; import { feed } from "./feed"; export const homepage = derive( [session, feed], (s, f) => ({ greeting: s.user ? `Welcome back, ${s.user.name}` : "Welcome", items: s.user ? f.items : f.items.slice(0, 5), }) ); derive only recomputes when one of its inputs changes — and only emits a notification when its output changes (by structural equality). It's the right tool for "computed views" or "memoized selectors". Slicing a store For very large stores, store.select() returns a slice that behaves like its own store: const currentUser = session.select((s) => s.user); currentUser.subscribe((u) => render(u)); // fires only when `s.user` changes — not on `expiresAt` changes Server-side rendering & serialization Every store can be serialized with store.toJSON() and rehydrated with store.fromJSON(). The intended flow on the server is: create stores, prime them with fetched data, render once, ship the dehydrated state along with the HTML. // server session.login(user, 3600_000); const html = renderToString(<App />); const state = { session: session.toJSON(), feed: feed.toJSON() }; // client session.fromJSON(state.session); feed.fromJSON(state.feed); hydrate(<App />); Testing stores Stores are easy to unit-test because they have no framework. Just call actions and assert against store.get(): import { session } from "./session"; beforeEach(() => session.reset()); test("login sets the user and expiry", () => { session.login({ id: 1, name: "Milena" }, 60_000); const s = session.get(); expect(s.user?.name).toBe("Milena"); expect(s.expiresAt).toBeGreaterThan(Date.now()); }); PREVIOUS ← Quickstart NEXT Actions & selectors → ON THIS PAGE Stores Creating a store Reading and subscribing Composing stores Slicing a store SSR & ser

The shape of the object you pass is the API of the store. import { forge } from "runeforge"; const session = forge({ state: { user: null as User | null, expiresAt: 0 }, actions: { login: (s, user: User, ttl: number) => ({ user, expiresAt: Date.now() + ttl }), logout: () => ({ user: null, expiresAt: 0 }), }, }); The returned store is a plain object with these methods, plus your actions as methods: MEMBER SIGNATURE DESCRIPTION get () => State Returns the current state (a frozen snapshot). set (next: Partial<State>) => void Imperative state update. Prefer actions in most cases. subscribe (listener) => unsubscribe Calls listener on every committed state change. select (selector) => SelectedView Returns a derived view that's its own subscribable store. reset () => void Returns to the initial state. Useful in tests. name string Auto-derived debug name, or passed via the options bag. Reading and subscribing The simplest store is read with get() and observed with subscribe(): const current = session.get(); // { user: null, expiresAt: 0 } const off = session.subscribe((next, prev) => { console.log("changed:", prev, "→", next); }); // later off(); State is immutable. Each commit replaces the previous state with a new frozen object. Don't try to mutate s.user.name = "x" — return a new object instead. Runeforge will warn in dev if it detects an in-place mutation. Composing stores Apps usually have several stores. They compose by importing each other and using derive(): import { derive } from "runeforge"; import { session } from "./session"; import { feed } from "./feed"; export const homepage = derive( [session, feed], (s, f) => ({ greeting: s.user ? `Welcome back, ${s.user.name}` : "Welcome", items: s.user ? f.items : f.items.slice(0, 5), }) ); derive only recomputes when one of its inputs changes — and only emits a notification when its output changes (by structural equality). It's the right tool for "computed views" or "memoized selectors". Slicing a store For very large stores, store.select() returns a slice that behaves like its own store: const currentUser = session.select((s) => s.user); currentUser.subscribe((u) => render(u)); // fires only when `s.user` changes — not on `expiresAt` changes Server-side rendering & serialization Every store can be serialized with store.toJSON() and rehydrated with store.fromJSON(). The intended flow on the server is: create stores, prime them with fetched data, render once, ship the dehydrated state along with the HTML. // server session.login(user, 3600_000); const html = renderToString(<App />); const state = { session: session.toJSON(), feed: feed.toJSON() }; // client session.fromJSON(state.session); feed.fromJSON(state.feed); hydrate(<App />); Testing stores Stores are easy to unit-test because they have no framework. Just call actions and assert against store.get(): import { session } from "./session"; beforeEach(() => session.reset()); test("login sets the user and expiry", () => { session.login({ id: 1, name: "Milena" }, 60_000); const s = session.get(); expect(s.user?.name).toBe("Milena"); expect(s.expiresAt).toBeGreaterThan(Date.now()); }); PREVIOUS ← Quickstart NEXT Actions & selectors → ON THIS PAGE Stores Creating a store Reading and subscribing Composing stores Slicing a store SSR & ser

observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools REFERENCE API reference Docs › Core concepts › Actions & selectors Core concept Actions & selectors. Actions describe how state changes. Selectors describe how state is read. Together they give you a one-way data flow without the ceremony of Redux. Actions An action is a function on a store. It receives the current state and any arguments you pass, and returns the next state — or a partial of it. const cart = forge({ state: { items: [] as Item[], coupon: null as string | null }, actions: { add: (s, item: Item) => ({ items: [...s.items, item] }), remove: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.filter(i => i.id !== id) }), apply: (s, code: string) => ({ coupon: code }), clear: () => ({ items: [], coupon: null }), }, }); // call them like methods cart.add({ id: 1, name: "Espresso", price: 3.50 }); cart.apply("BLOOM10"); Rules of thumb Return, don't mutate. Always return a new object. Spread, map, filter — but never assign in place. Return a partial. The partial is shallow-merged with current state, so you only return what changed. Stay synchronous if possible. Keep async work in effects (see the Async & effects guide). It makes actions trivially testable. Name actions for what they do, not how they do it. checkout() is better than setCheckoutState(true). Selectors A selector is a pure function from state to a derived value. Components — and any subscriber, really — use selectors so they only re-render when the value they care about changes. const totalPrice = (s: ReturnType<typeof cart.get>) => s.items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price, 0); cart.subscribe((s) => render(totalPrice(s))); // fires every change cart.select(totalPrice).subscribe(render); // fires only when total actually changes Composing selectors Selectors compose like any other pure functions. For more involved derivations across multiple stores, prefer derive() — it caches and only recomputes when its inputs change. import { derive } from "runeforge"; import { cart, coupons } from "./stores"; export const grandTotal = derive([cart, coupons], (c, cs) => { const sub = c.items.reduce((s, i) => s + i.price, 0); const off = c.coupon ? cs.discountFor(c.coupon) : 0; return { sub, discount: off, total: Math.max(0, sub - off) }; }); Reusable action creators For common patterns, Runeforge ships builder helpers like asyncSlice(), listSlice(), and formSlice(). They generate action sets so you don't write the same CRUD by hand. import { forge, listSlice } from "runeforge"; type Todo = { id: number; text: string; done: boolean }; export const todos = forge({ state: listSlice<Todo>().state, actions: listSlice<Todo>().actions("id"), }); // generated: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count todos.add({ id: 1, text: "Write docs", done: false }); todos.update(1, (t) => ({ done: true })); Action middleware Middleware wraps actions. Use it for logging, time-travel, persistence, and analytics. Middleware are pure functions that run before and after every commit. import { use } from "runeforge"; use((next) => (action, args) => { const t0 = performance.now(); const r = next(action, args); console.log(`${action.store}.${action.name}`, `${(performance.now() - t0).toFixed(1)}ms`); return r; }); The order is the order you call use() in. Devtools, persistence, and time-travel are all middleware — and you can write your own with the same signature. It receives the current state and any arguments you pass, and returns the next state — or a partial of it. const cart = forge({ state: { items: [] as Item[], coupon: null as string | null }, actions: { add: (s, item: Item) => ({ items: [...s.items, item] }), remove: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.filter(i => i.id !== id) }), apply: (s, code: string) => ({ coupon: code }), clear: () => ({ items: [], coupon: null }), }, }); // call them like methods cart.add({ id: 1, name: "Espresso", price: 3.50 }); cart.apply("BLOOM10"); Rules of thumb Return, don't mutate. Always return a new object. Spread, map, filter — but never assign in place. Return a partial. The partial is shallow-merged with current state, so you only return what changed. Stay synchronous if possible. Keep async work in effects (see the Async & effects guide). It makes actions trivially testable. Name actions for what they do, not how they do it. checkout() is better than setCheckoutState(true). Selectors A selector is a pure function from state to a derived value. Components — and any subscriber, really — use selectors so they only re-render when the value they care about changes. const totalPrice = (s: ReturnType<typeof cart.get>) => s.items.reduce((sum, i) => sum + i.price, 0); cart.subscribe((s) => render(totalPrice(s))); // fires every change cart.select(totalPrice).subscribe(render); // fires only when total actually changes Composing selectors Selectors compose like any other pure functions. For more involved derivations across multiple stores, prefer derive() — it caches and only recomputes when its inputs change. import { derive } from "runeforge"; import { cart, coupons } from "./stores"; export const grandTotal = derive([cart, coupons], (c, cs) => { const sub = c.items.reduce((s, i) => s + i.price, 0); const off = c.coupon ? cs.discountFor(c.coupon) : 0; return { sub, discount: off, total: Math.max(0, sub - off) }; }); Reusable action creators For common patterns, Runeforge ships builder helpers like asyncSlice(), listSlice(), and formSlice(). They generate action sets so you don't write the same CRUD by hand. import { forge, listSlice } from "runeforge"; type Todo = { id: number; text: string; done: boolean }; export const todos = forge({ state: listSlice<Todo>().state, actions: listSlice<Todo>().actions("id"), }); // generated: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count todos.add({ id: 1, text: "Write docs", done: false }); todos.update(1, (t) => ({ done: true })); Action middleware Middleware wraps actions. Use it for logging, time-travel, persistence, and analytics. Middleware are pure functions that run before and after every commit. import { use } from "runeforge"; use((next) => (action, args) => { const t0 = performance.now(); const r = next(action, args); console.log(`${action.store}.${action.name}`, `${(performance.now() - t0).toFixed(1)}ms`); return r; }); The order is the order you call use() in. Devtools, persistence, and time-travel are all middleware — and you can write your own with the same signature. observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☾ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) ☀ ★ 18.4k Docs › Examples Examples Apps you can fork. Self-contained example apps. Every one of them is under 500 lines and uses just the public API. Clone the repo, npm i, npm dev — that's the whole setup. All (12) Beginner Intermediate Advanced SSR beginner Counter (the canonical hello-world) The smallest possible Runeforge app. Single store, three actions, one component. React 34 LOC beginner Todo list with persistence Add / toggle / delete todos. State persists to localStorage with one option. React 88 LOC beginner Async fetcher with retry asyncSlice() pattern. Loads users with exponential-backoff retry on failure. Vue 3 110 LOC intermediate Multi-step form (typed) Uses formSlice() to manage values, errors, touched state, and submission. React 210 LOC intermediate Optimistic comments Show comments instantly, roll back on server error. Uses derive() + middleware. Solid 180 LOC intermediate Realtime presence WebSocket push updates per-user presence and merges into store. Svelte 5 240 LOC intermediate Routing-aware state Read URL params into a store; navigation is just an action. React 160 LOC advanced Undo / redo with snapshots Time-travel using built-in snapshot support. Cmd-Z / Cmd-Shift-Z. React 320 LOC advanced Server-side rendered shop Full SSR + hydration of multiple stores. Includes server-only state. React (Next 15) 460 LOC advanced Markdown editor with autosave Debounced autosave middleware, file-system adapter, and conflict detection. Vanilla JS 420 LOC advanced Spreadsheet with cross-cell formulas Each cell is a derived store; recompute graph triggered by edits. Solid 480 LOC advanced Drag-and-drop kanban (SSR) Move cards between columns; renders identically on server and client. React (Next 15) 440 LOC

observation.title: API reference — Runeforge
observation.visible_text: Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k REFERENCE Overview forge() derive() use() · middleware asyncSlice() listSlice() formSlice() devtools() REACT ADAPTER useStore() useSnapshot() <Provider /> (optional) ERRORS RF001 — RF019 OTHER Docs home Quickstart Examples Docs › API reference Reference · v3.4 API reference. Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

Every public symbol in runeforge and @runeforge/react. Re-export-only modules (runeforge/devtools, runeforge/utils) are linked at the bottom. FUNCTION forge(definition, options?) Available since v1.0 · Updated in v3.0 (action signature) Creates a store from a definition object. The shape of definition.state and definition.actions is inferred — TypeScript users get full autocomplete and type-checking with no extra annotations. SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

SIGNATURE function forge<S, A>( definition: { state: S; actions: A }, options?: { name?: string; persist?: boolean | PersistConfig } ): Store<S, A>; PARAMETERS NAME TYPE DESCRIPTION definition.state Object Initial state. Must be a plain object (or a value compatible with structuredClone). definition.actions Map<string, fn> Map of action functions. Each receives state as its first argument and may take any number of additional arguments. options.name string Override the auto-derived debug name. Visible in devtools and persisted storage keys. options.persist boolean | PersistConfig Persist this store to localStorage (or a custom adapter). See Persistence. RETURNS A Store<S, A> object with get(), set(), subscribe(), select(), reset(), toJSON(), fromJSON(), and all your action methods at the top level. EXAMPLE const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0, step: 1 }, actions: { inc: (s) => ({ count: s.count + s.step }), setStep: (s, step: number) => ({ step }), }, }, { name: "counter", persist: true }); Version history FUNCTION derive(inputs, fn) Available since v2.0 Creates a derived store from one or more input stores. fn runs only when at least one input has changed, and the result is shallow-compared before notifying subscribers — so identical outputs don't emit. SIGNATURE function derive<Inputs extends Store[], Out>( inputs: [...Inputs], fn: (...states: { [K in keyof Inputs]: StoreState<Inputs[K]> }) => Out ): DerivedStore<Out>; EXAMPLE const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => f.mode === "done" ? t.items.filter(x => x.done) : t.items ); Don't subscribe inside fn. A derive function must be pure and synchronous. Side effects (logging, fetching, subscribing) belong in an effect. FUNCTION use(middleware) Available since v2.4 Installs an action-level middleware. Middleware wrap every committed action across every store. Use this for logging, devtools, persistence, time-travel. function use(mw: (next: Dispatch) => Dispatch): () => void; use((next) => (action, args) => { console.log("→", action.name, args); return next(action, args); }); Calling use() returns a function that uninstalls the middleware. Middleware run in install order. HELPER asyncSlice<T>(options?) Available since v3.0 Returns { status, data, error } with the right types for async state. Designed to be spread into state alongside your own fields. const user = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice<User>(), lastFetch: 0 }, actions: { /* … */ }, }); HELPER listSlice<T>() Available since v3.1 Returns a state + actions pair for a keyed collection. The action set covers the common CRUD operations. { state: { items: T[] }, actions: (key: keyof T) => ListActions<T> } Generated actions: add, remove, replace, update, clear, byId, has, count. HELPER formSlice<T>() Available since v3.2 Adds values, errors, touched, submitting, and matching actions. Pair with a validation function for typed form state. MIDDLEWARE devtools(options?) Available since v1.0 Installs the Runeforge browser-devtools middleware. Renders an action log with diffs, supports "jump to" time-travel, and exposes per-store snapshots. devtools({ name: "My App", maxHistory: 200 }); React adapter (@runeforge/react

Runeforge v3.4 Docs API Examples Blog Community Search docs ⌘K v3.4 (latest) v3.3 v3.2 v2 (legacy) ☀ ★ 18.4k GETTING STARTED Introduction Quickstart (5 min) Why Runeforge? Installation Migration from Redux CORE CONCEPTS Stores Actions & selectors Subscriptions Composition & slicing Async & effects Persistence Devtools FRAMEWORK ADAPTERS React Solid Svelte 5 Vue 3 Vanilla JS / web components REFERENCE API reference Type definitions Errors Changelog Docs › Getting started › Quickstart Quickstart · 5 minutes From zero to a working app. In the next five minutes you'll install Runeforge, build a counter, build a todo list, and wire up an async fetcher. By the end you'll have used 90% of the API. Prerequisites: Node 20+ (or Bun). The examples use React but everything maps 1:1 to Solid, Svelte, Vue, and vanilla JS. Step 1 · Install Create a fresh app with whatever template you like. Then install Runeforge and the React adapter. # inside your app directory npm install runeforge @runeforge/react Step 2 · A counter store The smallest useful store has one piece of state and one action. Both are inferred from the object you pass to forge(). // stores/counter.ts import { forge } from "runeforge"; export const counter = forge({ state: { count: 0 }, actions: { increment: (s) => ({ count: s.count + 1 }), decrement: (s) => ({ count: s.count - 1 }), reset: () => ({ count: 0 }), }, }); Use it in a component with useStore: // Counter.tsx import { useStore } from "@runeforge/react"; import { counter } from "./stores/counter"; export function Counter() { const count = useStore(counter, (s) => s.count); return (

{count}

); } Notice three things: No provider. The store is just an import — it's already global. The component subscribes to a selector (s.count), not the whole store. If another part of state changed, this component would not re-render. Actions are called like ordinary methods. There's no dispatch(). Step 3 · A todo list (and a derived store) For richer state, use a slice for todos and another for the filter. Then derive a third store that combines them. // stores/todos.ts import { forge, derive } from "runeforge"; export const todos = forge({ state: { items: [] as { id: number; text: string; done: boolean }[] }, actions: { add: (s, text: string) => ({ items: [...s.items, { id: Date.now(), text, done: false }] }), toggle: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.map(t => t.id === id ? { ...t, done: !t.done } : t) }), remove: (s, id: number) => ({ items: s.items.filter(t => t.id !== id) }), clear: (s) => ({ items: s.items.filter(t => !t.done) }), }, }); export const filter = forge({ state: { mode: "all" as "all" | "active" | "done" }, actions: { setMode: (s, mode) => ({ mode }), }, }); // derive() runs only when its inputs change. export const visibleTodos = derive([todos, filter], (t, f) => { if (f.mode === "all") return t.items; if (f.mode === "active") return t.items.filter(x => !x.done); return t.items.filter(x => x.done); }); In the component, you subscribe to the derived store the same way you subscribe to a regular one: const visible = useStore(visibleTodos); return visible.map(t => ); Step 4 · Async (the easy way) Async work belongs in effects. Effects can read and write any store, await whatever they want, and report status into a status field. Runeforge ships an asyncSlice() helper that gives you a typed status object for free. import { forge, asyncSlice } from "runeforge"; export const users = forge({ state: { ...asyncSlice() }, actions: { async load(s) { if (s.status === "loading") return s; try { const r = await fetch("/api/users"); const data = await r.json(); return { status: "ready", data, error: null }; } catch (e) { return { status: "error", data: null, error: e.message }; } }, }, }); Inside the component: const { status, data, err
